## Sequenced expectations (MEASURED during this replay, in release order)

Every line below was printed by the migration itself while running in the REAL RELEASE
SEQUENCE on the restored production shape -- not typed by an author, and not measured by
running that migration on its own.

That distinction is the entire point. Migration 537 revokes TRUNCATE from authenticated on
214 tables when applied by itself -- its own header says exactly that -- but on MORE than
214 in this sequence, because migration 534 creates cron_run_log three steps earlier and
the new table inherits the schema default that still includes TRUNCATE. An operator
reading a hard-coded 214 would see the larger number, conclude the run had gone wrong,
and stop a CORRECT release.

A hard-coded count is the same defect class as migration 477 static REVOKE list: a number
generated against one shape and asserted against another. Derive it, or do not print it.

## Candidate accounting — every candidate in exactly one bucket, and they must SUM

```
considered (candidates at or below the ceiling)     703
  OK                  (ledger + catalogue agree)    242
  APPLIED             (replayed by this rehearsal)     15
  LEDGER_ONLY         (catalogue-driven, row only)      1
  DECIDED_LEDGER_ONLY (decision, row only, guarded)      1
  SHAPE_TOLERATED     (failed, declared, still OPEN)      2
  SKIPPED_BY_DECISION (never run at all, CLOSED)      3
  LEDGER_LIES         (pre-declared, untouched)      36
  UNVERIFIABLE        (row exists, no catalogue signal)    403
  REFUSED             (plan entries never attempted)      0
  ---- sum                                          703
```

SHAPE_TOLERATED and SKIPPED_BY_DECISION are NOT the same bucket and must never be summed
together. The first is a migration that FAILED on this shape and whose disposition is still
an open question for a human. The second was never attempted at all, because a human closed
the question before this run started -- release/config/decided-migrations.txt names the
decision behind each one. Conflating them reports an open risk as a settled one.

UNVERIFIABLE is the honest weak spot of catalogue-over-ledger, and it is large. Those
versions have a ledger row and NO catalogue signal at all -- function-only, grant-only and
data-only migrations that docs/missions/prodprep/ledger-evidence.sh cannot probe. For them
this rehearsal trusts the ledger, which is the very thing migration 477 proved can lie.
## VERDICT: PASS
